key_insight: A localized hybrid FEM–random feature approach can solve elliptic interface problems on unfitted meshes by using standard finite elements away from the interface and random features only in the narrow cut-cell band.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the high cost of global surrogate representations while preserving accuracy for challenging multi-physics interface problems with coefficient jumps, irregular geometries, and high contrast.
method: Use standard Qp FEM on uncut background cells.
Use local random-feature representations only in interface-cut cells on both physical sides of the interface.
Enforce jump and flux conditions on the true interface, then couple FEM and RFM across an artificial grid-aligned interface via residual constraints and Schur reduction.
evidence_signal: The method is numerically evaluated in 2D and 3D on high-contrast, nonsmooth, multiple-interface, and irregular-boundary problems, including a thermal-homogenization application.
watch_item: The approach adds implementation complexity because it requires accurate interface localization, residual coupling across two interfaces, and efficient sparse elimination for the interior FEM unknowns.
paper_title: A Localized Hybrid Finite Element--Random Feature Method for Elliptic Interface Problems on Unfitted Meshes
